subject: Pricing exhibit questions: degressivity, bandwash carveouts and operational playbook
messages:
From: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@blueskyanalytics.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exhibit — degressivity and bandwash questions

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement here at BlueSky has a couple of specific asks on the pricing exhibit before we push to legal:

1) Degressivity model: our procurement team wants confirmation that stepped discounts (degressivity) will apply on the committed band only (i.e., not retroactively into prior months) and we'd like an explicit smoothing/window that prevents abrupt cliffing when moving bands. Can Redwood propose operational language?

2) Bandwash carveout: for pilot volumes (first 90 days) we need a carveout so the floor does not trigger on pilot traffic spikes. We are open to a pilot true-up but want it excluded from annual minimum enforcement.

3) Billing timing: agreement on true-up cadence (quarterly vs annual) and whether overage credit can be used toward future months.

Attached is our RFP terminology doc to align definitions.

Can we get a proposed redline and a quick note on how you normally operationalize band transitions so our finance folks can sign off?

Best,
Emily
Emily Sanders
Head of Procurement, BlueSky Analytics
Attachments: BlueSky_RFP_Terminology.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — degressivity and bandwash questions

Hi Emily — thanks, clear asks.

Short answers up front:
- Degressivity: we can make discounts apply prospectively on band movement and add a 60–90 day smoothing window to avoid cliffs.
- Pilot carveout: reasonable — proposal would be to exclude an initial 90-day pilot from minimum-commit calculations, with a one-time pro-rated true-up to the first quarter if usage exceeds pilot expectations.
- True-up cadence: we usually suggest quarterly true-ups for mid-market deals, annual for enterprise; open to quarterly here given your ramp shape.

I'm looping in Karthik (pricing) and Marissa (legal ops) to draft the exhibit redline and an operational playbook we can include in the SOW. Expect a redline by EOD Thursday.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday 4/16 to align with finance?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding BlueSky's procurement note. Key asks: degressivity behavior, pilot carveout (90 days), true-up cadence and overage credit policy.

Please draft:
- A redline of the pricing exhibit with: explicit prospectivity language for degressivity, a 60–90 day smoothing window, pilot carveout clause (exclude pilot from annual minimum; one-time pro-rata true-up to first quarter), and a definition for "bandwash" (how we reconcile variance between committed and actual).
- A short operational playbook (bullet list) that covers: detection/notification of band movement, auto-notify thresholds, billing rights for overage vs crediting, and runbook for customer-initiated ramp reversions.

Attaching an internal working draft — please add line edits and track alternate language. We'll aim to present a single consolidated redline to Emily + BlueSky legal on Friday.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing exhibit — degressivity and bandwash questions (action: redline & ops playbook)

Laura / Marissa — wrote up suggested compromise language and operational bullets below (quick notes):

1) Degressivity prospectivity (proposed exhibit language): "Discount steps shall apply prospectively from the first billing cycle following the end of the smoothing window triggered by a committed band change; no retroactive application to prior billing cycles."

2) Smoothing window: 60 days recommended. Rationale: balances BlueSky's ramp flexibility and Redwood's forecasting. We can offer 90 days as a concession if BlueSky agrees to a soft cap on burst credits during pilot.

3) Pilot carveout: add clause: "Pilot volumes (defined as the first 90 days following initial production cutover) are excluded from the calculation of Annual Minimum Commit; Customer shall perform a one-time pro-rata true-up at the end of the first full fiscal quarter post-cutover if pilot volumes materially exceed forecast (>150% of forecasted pilot volume)."

4) Overages & credits: operationally, allow one-time application of overage credits to subsequent monthly invoices within the same quarter; any remaining credit applies to next quarter only. No carry beyond 12 months.

5) Bandwash/runbook bullets (operational playbook):
- Notification: automated email at 80% and 100% of new band threshold; account ops owner assigned for final confirmation.
- Reconciliation: monthly automatic reconciliation; customer can request manual review within 15 days of invoice.
- Rollback policy: if usage drops >40% below new band for 2 consecutive months within smoothing window, rollback to prior band is permitted once per 12-month period.

I've added redline to the doc (see attached). If Marissa can give legal thumbs-up on the phrasing (especially the >150% materiality trigger and rollback carve), we can send to BlueSky with the operational playbook and a short cover note.

Karthik
VP, Pricing Strategy, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Pricing exhibit — degressivity and bandwash questions

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear ask and patience. Attached is an updated pricing exhibit (RDW-BlueSky-Exhibit-v3.pdf) and a short operational playbook. High-level summary of what we propose:

- Degressivity applies prospectively (no retroactive discounting); proposed smoothing window = 60 days (we can extend to 90 days if you accept a temporary restriction on pilot burst credits).
- Pilot carveout: first 90 days excluded from Annual Minimum Commit; one-time pro-rata true-up to the first full fiscal quarter if pilot >150% of forecast.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups for Year 1, moving to annual thereafter; overage credits may be applied within-quarter and up to one quarter forward, not beyond 12 months.
- Operational playbook attached: notification thresholds, reconciliation runbook, rollback policy (single allowed rollback per 12-month window).

Next steps: please review the PDF redline and the playbook. If acceptable, we'll open a DocuSign envelope to incorporate the exhibit and SOW updates. I'm happy to join a quick call Thursday 4/22 with finance if you'd like to finalize.
